finding.claim: list_users_sorted() concatenates the attacker-controlled $_GET['sort'] directly into an ORDER BY clause of an unprepared query, allowing SQL injection (boolean/time-free blind extraction of arbitrary data via subqueries in ORDER BY).
finding.source: list.php:5 $_GET['sort'] (HTTP query string, fully attacker-controlled; ?? 'id' applies only when the parameter is missing)
finding.sink: list.php:6 $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort)

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id'; attacker supplies any string via the sort parameter
$sort concatenated into the SQL string with no validation, cast, or escaping; executed via unprepared PDO::query()

ORDER BY accepts arbitrary expressions in SQLite, including CASE and scalar subqueries, so the attacker can reference other tables (e.g. (CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(secret,1,1) FROM other_table LIMIT 1)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)) and infer data from row ordering in the result

finding.guards_checked: (1) No allowlist or type check on $_GET['sort'] (line 5 uses only ?? default). (2) No intval/ctype/regex validation. (3) Not parameterized: PDO prepared statements cannot bind identifiers or ORDER BY expressions, so using prepare() would not have fixed this; an allowlist would. (4) No escaping of the concatenated value. (5) No authentication or authorization check visible in this file; exploitability over HTTP depends on whether list_users_sorted() is routed from a web endpoint, which is not present in the repo. Note: list_users_safe() on lines 9-13 uses an allowlist and is not affected; find_user() on lines 15-19 uses a bound parameter and is not affected.

verdict.guard_found: none. list.php:5 applies only a `?? 'id'` default, with no allowlist, cast, or validation. list.php:6 concatenates $sort into the query and runs it through unprepared $pdo->query(). The safe alternatives are list_users_safe() at lines 9-13 (allowlist at line 11), which is not affected, and find_user() at lines 15-19 (bound parameter), which is not affected. The repo contains no caller of list_users_sorted(), so no route or auth check is visible.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: $_GET['sort'] at list.php:5 flows unvalidated into the query at list.php:6, and no guard exists in the file. However, list.php defines list_users_sorted() but never calls it, and the repo has no web endpoint or auth layer that invokes it, so I cannot confirm an attacker can reach this sink over HTTP.
